title: Obernberger See Wipptal
highlights: Pristine high-alpine lake at 1,590 meters altitude within a protected landscape area
Picturesque pilgrimage chapel Maria am See situated on a wooded island
Breathtaking views of the rugged dolomite towers of the Obernberger Tribulaun
Cherished family hiking destination across gentle alpine pastures and open larch woods
kurzbeschreibung: The Obernberger See in the Wipptal is an idyllic mountain lake with an island chapel beneath the rugged rock faces of the Tribulaun.
beschreibung:
Tranquil Mountain Idyll at the Brenner

The Obernberger See lies at the end of the pristine Obernbergtal in the Tyrolean Wipptal at 1,590 metres above sea level. Framed by dense larch forests and the mighty limestone pinnacles of the Obernberger Tribulaun, it is considered one of the most untouched mountain lakes in the Eastern Alps.

Island Chapel and Shoreline Paths

A historic wooden bridge leads to the picturesque peninsula with the pilgrimage chapel Maria am See, built in the 18th century. Swimming is prohibited to protect the delicate alpine ecosystem, yet the circular lakeside path offers incomparable views of the crystal-clear mountain water shimmering in all shades of blue and green.
